title: Cost Model API v1 — Optimize field requirements (working doc)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- Optimize needs to compute ROI and provide “what-if” cost projections (batching, caching, quantization) using the new Standard Cost Model (SCM) spec + Cost Model API.
- This is a working requirements capture for Cost Model API v1 from Optimize’s perspective: required fields, confidence/guardrails needs, and open questions.
- Goal is to align early with Platform/Telemetry on what is feasible for v1 (Q1 2026) vs what must land in v2.

Owners / reviewers
- Owner: Aditya Rao (Optimize product)
- What-if methodology: Jonas Weber
- Modeling inputs: Hassan Mirza (caching/batching), Arjun Desai (quant), Maya Srinivasan (Applied ML sponsor)
- Platform/implementation: Ethan Park
- Telemetry contracts: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman

Primary Optimize use-cases (v1)
1) Recommendation ROI cards (in-product)
- Example: “Enable prefix/KV caching for route X” → projected savings $/day and % cost reduction, with risk/confidence.
- Example: “Increase target batch size / enable continuous batching profile Y” → cost delta + latency delta.
- Example: “Switch quantization profile fp16 → int8 (profile_id=…)” → cost delta with quality guardrail notes.

2) What-if sandbox (internal first)
- Input a workload summary for a route/model and evaluate a few candidate configs.
- Used by Solutions Eng + internal support to sanity-check a customer’s expectations.

3) Backtesting + regression
- Replay “golden” workloads and ensure savings estimates aren’t systematically optimistic.
- Used to debug drift and assumptions (see SUP-31877).

Non-goals for v1 (Optimize-side)
- Full automated exploration across huge parameter spaces.
- Customer-visible pricing calculator.
- Real-time per-request synchronous what-if on the hot request path (Optimize can tolerate seconds-level latency for what-if endpoints if bounded).

Key requirement: outputs must be decomposable
Optimize needs SCM outputs in a structured breakdown so that we can:
- Explain savings drivers (e.g., “decode GPU cost decreased due to higher batch efficiency” vs “overhead allocation changed”).
- Avoid recommendations where savings come from accounting changes rather than real runtime improvements.

============================================================
A) Minimum required API outputs for Optimize (v1)
============================================================

A1. Common identifiers (required)
- cost_model_version: string (schema version used)
- request_id: string (for tracing / debug; can be generated by caller)
- organization_id / tenant_id: required for multi-tenant correctness
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private (string)
- region: string (e.g., us-east-1)
- environment: prod | staging | dev
- model_id: stable ID from model catalog
- model_version: pinned serving version (string)
- quantization_profile_id: stable profile identifier (even if “fp16-default”)

A2. Cost outputs (required)
We need both absolute and normalized outputs.
- total_cost_usd: total estimated cost for the measurement window (or per-request) in USD
- total_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: normalized cost (for UI consistency)
- total_cost_per_request_usd: if request-level estimate
- breakdown_by_stage (prefill vs decode):
  - prefill_cost_usd
  - decode_cost_usd
- breakdown_by_resource (must be stable across versions):
  - gpu_cost_usd
  - cpu_cost_usd (if non-trivial; ok if 0 for some deployments)
  - memory_cost_usd (optional; see open questions)
  - network_cost_usd (optional; likely v2)
  - overhead_cost_usd (see ADR-022; must be clearly defined)
- “attributable_cost_usd” vs “allocated_overhead_usd” split (strongly preferred for v1)
  - We need this to avoid recommendations that look good due to overhead allocation artifacts.

A3. Token and request accounting outputs (required)
We need “what counted” fields for explainability + debugging.
- input_tokens: integer
- output_tokens: integer
- total_tokens: integer
- billable_input_tokens: integer (if different)
- billable_output_tokens: integer (if different)
- prefill_tokens: integer (often ~input_tokens but not always due to system tokens / tool wrappers)
- decode_tokens: integer (often ~output_tokens)

A4. Performance / utilization summary (required, bounded)
Optimize uses these to explain *why* cost changes.
- avg_batch_size_prefill: float
- avg_batch_size_decode: float
- batch_efficiency_score: float (0..1), definition stable
- queue_time_ms_p50/p95: optional but useful (latency vs throughput tradeoffs)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: float (0..1)
- kv_cache_bytes_saved: optional (nice-to-have)

A5. Confidence / quality guardrails (required for what-if)
We need guardrails so Optimize doesn’t present overconfident savings.
- estimate_confidence: low | medium | high (or numeric 0..1)
- confidence_interval_low_usd / confidence_interval_high_usd (preferred; can be omitted for v1 if too heavy)
- assumptions: list of short strings (e.g., “cache warm-rate assumed 80%”, “batching limited by max_seq_len=4096”)
- invalid_reason / warning_codes: list (e.g., “WORKLOAD_OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION”, “TELEMETRY_LAGGED”, “PARAM_OUT_OF_RANGE”)

============================================================
B) What-if scenarios Optimize needs (v1)
============================================================

We want a small set of supported scenario types with strict bounds. Avoid free-form knobs that explode compute or cardinality.

B0. General what-if contract (shared)
Inputs:
- baseline_workload_summary (or baseline_cost_input) provided by caller OR referenced by a saved “workload_id”.
- proposed_config_change: one of the supported scenario types below.
Outputs:
- baseline_cost (same schema as A2)
- proposed_cost (same schema as A2)
- delta_cost_usd and delta_percent
- drivers: list of top contributors (bounded to N=5)
- confidence + warnings (A5)

B1. Batching what-if (v1)
Supported knobs (proposed):
- target_max_batch_size_decode: integer (bounded; e.g., 1..64)
- target_max_batch_size_prefill: integer (bounded)
- continuous_batching_enabled: bool
- scheduling_policy_id: string (optional; can be “default”)

Required outputs for batching scenario:
- projected_avg_batch_size_prefill/decode
- projected_batch_efficiency_score
- projected_latency_impact_ms_p50/p95 (optional; v1 might return “unknown” with warning)

Notes:
- Runtime team (Sofia/Omar) flagged that some batching metrics are not stable across kernels; Optimize can tolerate an abstract efficiency score if definition is stable.

B2. Caching what-if (v1)
Supported knobs (proposed):
- caching_mode: off | prefix_only | kv_prefix (string)
- cache_eviction_policy: lru | ttl | adaptive (optional)
- cache_ttl_seconds: integer (optional; bounds)

We need at least one of the following in v1:
Option 1 (simpler): caller provides expected cache_hit_rate (workload-dependent)
Option 2 (more “platform-owned”): API estimates cache_hit_rate from workload summary + historicals

Optimize preference:
- v1 supports Option 1 to ship quickly; but must label as assumption.
- v2 adds Option 2 once telemetry + workload fingerprints are trustworthy.

Required outputs for caching scenario:
- assumed_or_projected_kv_cache_hit_rate
- delta_prefill_tokens_processed (if caching reduces prefill compute)
- drivers: should attribute savings to prefill vs decode clearly

B3. Quantization what-if (v1)
Supported knobs (proposed):
- quantization_profile_id: string (required)
- allowed_quality_risk: conservative | balanced | aggressive (optional; maps to guardrails)

Required outputs for quantization scenario:
- projected_throughput_multiplier (optional but very useful for ROI explanation)
- projected_gpu_cost_delta_usd
- quality_risk_notes: short string (e.g., “Profile int8-rtxA10 validated for summarization; tool-calling may regress”) — can be coarse for v1

Important: Quant uncertainty
- We need at least a warning/flag when a quant profile is outside validated eval coverage.
- See Slack eng-ml thread on uncertainty representation. We can ship with categorical confidence + warning codes in v1.

============================================================
C) Workload summary inputs Optimize can provide (v1)
============================================================

We can’t (and shouldn’t) send per-request traces to the what-if endpoint.

Proposed “WorkloadSummary” fields (caller-provided)
- route_id: string (Redwood route / endpoint identifier)
- window_start / window_end: timestamps (or “last_24h”) 
- requests: integer
- input_tokens_p50/p90/p99: integers
- output_tokens_p50/p90/p99: integers
- total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens: integers
- max_seq_len_observed: integer
- tool_call_rate: float (0..1) (optional)
- streaming_rate: float (0..1) (optional)
- concurrency_p50/p95: integer (optional)

Why we need distribution (not just averages)
- Batching and kernel selection sensitivity to tail seq lengths.
- Caching sensitivity to prompt repetition (not captured well by averages).

If v1 can’t support full distributions
- Accept p50/p95 only; mark confidence lower.

============================================================
D) Field-level requirements table (v1)
============================================================

Legend: P0 must-have for Optimize v1; P1 strongly preferred; P2 v2 likely

| Field | Priority | Why Optimize needs it | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| cost_model_version | P0 | Debug + consistency across releases | Must be in every response |
| model_id / model_version | P0 | Tie projections to pinned serving version | Required for reproducibility |
| quantization_profile_id | P0 | Quant what-if + explain baseline | Even if default |
| deployment_mode / region | P0 | Costs differ by SKU + allocation rules | Also impacts overhead |
| total_cost_usd | P0 | ROI headline | For window or per-request |
| total_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | P0 | UI normalization | Avoids confusion across token volumes |
| prefill_cost_usd / decode_cost_usd | P0 | Savings explanation | Must be stable semantics |
| gpu_cost_usd | P0 | Primary lever in ROI | If impossible, total still required |
| overhead_cost_usd | P0 | Avoid misleading recs | Must be defined (allocated vs attributable) |
| attributable_cost_usd | P1 | Better ROI signal | If not available, document limitations |
| input_tokens / output_tokens | P0 | Normalize, validate accounting | Needed to catch weirdness |
| kv_cache_hit_rate | P1 | Caching ROI driver | If caller-provided, label assumption |
| avg_batch_size_prefill/decode | P1 | Batching ROI driver | Caller can’t infer reliably |
| batch_efficiency_score | P0 | Explain batching improvements | Stable definition required |
| estimate_confidence | P0 | UI + guardrails | Categorical ok |
| warning_codes | P0 | Don’t show unsafe recs | Must be machine-readable |
| confidence_interval_usd | P2 | Better decisioning | Could be expensive to compute |
| latency_impact_p95 | P2 | Avoid SLO violations | For v1 can be “unknown” |
| network_cost_usd | P2 | Some private deployments | Likely v2 |

============================================================
E) Open questions (v1 vs v2)
============================================================

E1. How should overhead be represented?
- Need a consistent split: request-attributable vs allocated overhead.
- Question: is overhead returned as a single bucket or multiple (e.g., “control_plane”, “idle_capacity”, “support/SRE”)?
- Optimize preference for v1: single overhead bucket + clear definition + an “allocation_policy_id” string.

E2. What is the unit of computation for what-if?
- Per-request vs per-window.
- Optimize preference: per-window using WorkloadSummary; also return normalized $/1k tokens.

E3. Should what-if assume fixed demand or fixed capacity?
- Batching can increase throughput; savings depends on whether we keep same latency SLO or same GPU pool.
- Optimize preference:
  - v1: assume fixed demand (same request volume), estimate per-token cost change.
  - v2: add modes: fixed_capacity, fixed_latency_budget.

E4. Cache warm-rate vs cache hit-rate
- Support ticket SUP-31877: ROI inflated due to unrealistic cache assumptions.
- We need a standard definition:
  - warm_rate: fraction of requests that see a “warm cache state” (session/prefix already present)
  - hit_rate: conditional hits given warm state
- Platform pushback (Slack eng-platform/1769267448) suggests keeping v1 simple.
- Proposal:
  - v1 input: expected_kv_cache_hit_rate (single scalar) + warning if not provided.
  - v2: separate warm_rate and hit_rate (or provide a richer workload fingerprint).

E5. Quantization quality guardrails
- Do we want the Cost Model API to return quality risk metadata, or should Optimize fetch from Evals service separately?
- Preference:
  - v1: Cost Model returns warning_codes like QUANT_PROFILE_NOT_EVAL_VALIDATED_FOR_TASK.
  - v2: integrated “quality_constraint” block with task tags + eval coverage summary.

E6. Cardinality/bounds
- We need to agree on a bounded driver list (e.g., top 5 drivers) and bounded breakdown dimensions.
- Avoid returning per-layer/kernel-level details in API response.

============================================================
F) UX implications / how Optimize will use these fields
============================================================

F1. Recommendation card
- Headline: “Estimated savings: $X/day (Y%)”
- Subtext: “Confidence: medium” + “Assumptions: cache hit rate 70%”
- Explain: “Savings primarily from reduced prefill GPU time (cache hits)” or “higher decode batch efficiency”.
- Always show warnings when present.

F2. Guardrails
Optimize should suppress or require user confirmation when:
- estimate_confidence=low
- warning_codes includes WORKLOAD_OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION or PARAM_OUT_OF_RANGE
- overhead dominates delta (e.g., >50% of projected savings comes from overhead change)

============================================================
G) Near-term action items
============================================================

1) Confirm v1 required fields with Platform (Ethan) and Telemetry (Logan/Nadia)
- Specifically: attributable vs overhead split, stable batch_efficiency definition.

2) Decide caching what-if v1 approach (caller-provided hit rate vs platform-estimated)
- If caller-provided, define how Optimize will estimate it from limited telemetry.

3) Provide example payloads
- I will draft 2-3 example WorkloadSummary inputs and expected what-if outputs for:
  - caching on a summarization route
  - batching on chat route (long-tail seq lengths)
  - quant profile change on embeddings reranker

4) Align terminology with SCM ADRs
- Ensure “prefill/decode” semantics match runtime export and ADR-022 taxonomy.

Appendix: Notes from recent threads
- eng-ml/1768474332: agreement that v1 can ship with categorical confidence + warning codes; CI intervals not required if too costly.
- product/1768589014: Console wants consistent breakdown; Optimize wants what-if; both agreed taxonomy is shared.
- SUP-31877: key lesson: if caching assumptions are caller-provided, must be visible in UI and included in response assumptions[] so we can audit.
